detailed_explanation_blocks.text: The STAC/OGC watcher boundary in [Ideas-04-19] is described as a surface that polls external STAC catalogs (and, where supported, listens on webhook endpoints) for changes to upstream collections that KFM cares about. The watcher is read-mostly: it observes but does not write to upstream catalogs; its outputs are local artifacts that downstream stages process. The watcher's discipline is also narrowly scoped: it watches only catalogs explicitly registered with KFM, never crawls discoverable catalogs without registration, and never extends its scope based on links discovered in fetched content. The boundary discipline is what keeps the watcher governable: a watcher that discovers and follows links would have an unbounded surface and could not be made fail-closed. The corpus is honest that this is PROPOSED rather than CONFIRMED - no watcher is shown implemented - but the design is consistent with the rest of the WCH posture. Synthesis weight: high in design terms; the watcher is the system's primary external interface and its discipline determines what the trust membrane means in practice. Tensions: webhooks are not universally supported, and a polling watcher has its own latency profile; the corpus mentions but does not pin down the polling cadence per catalog. Related ideas: KFM-IDX-RUN-002, KFM-IDX-WCH-002, KFM-IDX-WCH-005. Expansion direction: a watcher specification (registered catalogs, polling cadence, webhook handlers, scope limits) that is itself versioned.
